comparison_evidence.quote: Rule: any somatic/beat phrase appearing more than 3 times per book is a defect — including new phrases invented to replace an old one. Fixing a tic with a fresh repeated phrase is the same defect wearing a different coat; vary the replacement or cut the beat. ... "the way you/he/she [verb]..." as a simile engine — cap the *identical* construction at 3 per chapter

findings.consequence: Carried forward from r1 unrepaired. Counted over the repaired draft: 'six days' is 6, unchanged from r1 (identical lines, and twice inside l.69); the 'as a man/woman [verb]' simile engine is 5 against r1's 6, and the single reduction is the instance at the old l.87 that the CH13-014 repair deleted incidentally, not a pass over the engine. Five instances of one construction in a 3,995-word chapter, four of them making the same rhetorical move (an abstract man invoked to certify a gesture), is the watermark the charter caps at three; the repeated 'for six days' tenure clause is a second one. The author's r2 report lists no repair against this finding. Because the notice, the warning and the close all sit in the last quarter, l.107's 'as a man nods' is the last simile a listener hears before the ending, which is where the pattern is least affordable.

draft_evidence.quote: Cael took the log out, before he went up the last flight, because a thing that has come should be entered where it came ... He read it once, in the plain hand, in a chamber under a city, with a man across the table who had just given him a thing by working in front of him and had then, deliberately, looked away from him ... He let it stand, and did not look at the place in himself where the eleven went round, and closed the log. // The eyes paid on the last flight.

comparison_evidence.quote: He went back to the carving. ... Vastin was on the landing when Cael came up to it with the lamp, after ... and Cael took the case's other strap without a word and they went up the stair together ... The man said, on the fourth flight, without looking round: "You told him." ... and they went up.

findings.consequence: The approved resequencing moved the notice and the log's close out of the chamber and onto the stair, but the paragraph that carries them still locates the act in the chamber. Cael has left Cleon at l.93, taken the case with Vastin at l.97, climbed to the fourth flight by l.99, and takes the log out at l.109 'before he went up the last flight' — and l.113 then reads the entry 'in a chamber under a city, with a man across the table'. On the page a careful reader may recover it as a description of where the fragment came from; read aloud a listener has just been placed on a stair with Vastin two paragraphs running and hears the boy put back at Cleon's table. It is the one seam left by the move, and it sits in the paragraph immediately before the close.
findings.repair_target: Line 113 — re-point the locative to the stair, or convert it to the past ('in the plain hand, on a stair, for a man who had just given him a thing by working in front of him'). comparison_evidence.quote: Cael did not say anything for a while. Then he said, "It's entered," and took the log out, on the step, and wrote it, and did not tell the man what else he had entered, because a fragment is a thing you own and a thing a man gave you is a thing you owe.

findings.consequence: The CH13-003 repair is correct in its load — the eleventh is now entered-not-told and the debt stands, which is what Ch12 shows — but the rationale clause it arrives with reads against Ch12's own words. Ch12 ends on Cael making the ledger entry Vastin asked for, on the step, in front of him: 'It's entered.' Ch13 says 'the only currency the man took was a ledger and the entry was not yet made.' A reader coming straight off Ch12's last page has that sentence in the ear. The referent is arguably a different entry — the one that would record the telling — but nothing on the page distinguishes them, and this is the paragraph the chapter uses to argue its covenant has never been broken, so the reader is already reading it closely.
findings.repair_target: Line 59 — name which entry is missing ('the entry that would have said what else he took was not yet made'), or drop the ledger clause and let 'that debt stood' carry it. Do not disturb the clause the repair added at the end of the sentence; it is what closes CH13-003.

concerns: The 140-word sentence at l.115 ('Cleon had said they would ... and when the smear went back to a lamp they went up') is now the longest in the chapter, ahead of l.49's 133 and l.11's 114, and it is the last paragraph before the fixed close. It carries no dialogue turns and it is the house voice's earned accumulating mode doing real work — it is the cost the notice promised and the r1 concern asked for — so I am not raising it. Flagged because the ear reaches the ending having just carried the notice, the log's close and this; if a later compression pass wants one break, it belongs after 'and it was his now:'.

CH13-004's repaired value at l.113 is 'the eleven', taken after the notice for the twelfth has rendered two paragraphs above. The r1 repair target authorised either value, and 'the eleven' is defensible (the twelfth is on the page, not yet gone round) — but STATE_RUNNING will inherit whichever number is written here, so the splice should record the reading deliberately rather than by transcription.

CH13-006's repair loosens Cleon's promise to 'when I've finished the week' (l.19) and 'in a day or two ... at the week's end' (l.33), which is exactly what the r1 repair target asked for and lets Ch15 pay it. Note that l.21 still fixes the demonstration on 'the sixth day of his week', so 'the week's end' reads at first pass as the 292nd — Ch14, which carries no Cleon scene. 'in a day or two' rescues it. If the planning seat wants the promise unambiguous, the cheapest fix is to drop 'at the week's end' from l.33 and leave 'in a day or two' to carry the date alone.

Vastin's 'You told him.' and 'He looked away.' (ll.99-103) still name two things he did not witness — he takes the case and goes at l.63, before the telling. The r1 draft wrapped the inference framing around the exchange; the CH13-010 repair correctly broke the turns out, which pushes the framing ('as a man nods who has spent forty years watching people be told things') to l.107, four short paragraphs after the first claim. It still lands, and Cael's confirmations make the lines read as probes. One clause on l.99 would close it for free if that line is touched again.

The handcart at l.3 is no longer contradicted — the paragraph in which Cael carried a box up the stair by hand is deleted — but it is still a prop introduced for one line and never seen again at the yard door. Ch14/Ch16/Ch17 will inherit the question of whether it is still borrowed.

'six days' as the lamp count (ll.25, 65, 69) indexes off Cleon's week, while Vastin's 'six days of watching Cael' (l.15) and the lamp-reach tally at l.53 ('four, on the fourth day; two, today') index off Vastin's own tenure, and Vastin came down as a hand on the 284th, which makes the 291st his eighth day. Unchanged from r1. Whatever repair takes CH13-009 should put every count on one clock rather than only thinning the phrase.

The r1 concern that the notice promised a cost the chapter never paid is resolved and is now one of the chapter's better beats: l.115 spends the eyes on the last flight, in the dark, with Vastin declining to offer a hand. Record it as a strength before any compression pass reads it as expansion padding and takes it back out.
strengths: The repair is surgical. Six changed regions, every one a named repair target, no unrelated passage rewritten, and all eight recorded r1 strengths intact — the record-sits/instruction-leans exposition (l.27), the acquisition carried on Cleon's breath (l.31), 'He knew the moment this time' and the floor-leaning paragraph (ll.43-47), Karis's own finding (l.37), the refusal at l.49, 'No. I'll not say that one.' (l.85), the look-away read as the covenant's other half (l.113), and the clerk's arithmetic (ll.9-11).

The resequenced tail is better than a repair. Moving the climb between the warning and the close puts the chapter's stair image — planted at l.27 ('you can feel the order as you can feel which way a stair goes in the dark by where the treads are') and called at l.33 ('This is a stair') — inside a literal dark stair the boy cannot see the treads of. The blocker's fix produced the chapter's best structural rhyme.

The eye-cost at l.115 is the single most valuable thing the repair added: the notice's 'Costs the eyes, after' is discharged within twenty lines, in the dark, on a stair, with Vastin 'a step above him' who 'said nothing, and waited, and did not offer a hand, because the man had learned in a week what a hand was worth to a boy on a stair.' It pays a system promise and advances the Vastin thread in the same breath, and it does it without a word of comment.

Breaking the four turns out (ll.99-107) is the right repair and not merely a formatting one. 'You told him.' / 'I told him.' / 'He looked away.' / 'Yes.' as four bare paragraphs on a stair is the whole Vastin relationship in eleven words, and it now reads aloud as four voices instead of one clause chain.

l.87's replacement — 'He looked at the boy a moment longer, and did not say it.' — is a better line than the gesture it removed. The look-back is now spent once, at the fixed 'He went back to the carving.', exactly as the card stages it, and the restraint at l.87 makes the later gesture land as a decision rather than a repetition.

l.89's cup preamble now ends on 'He picked it up now, and drank.', which leaves the setting-down to the fixed line and restores the pause the card built. Thirty years of a clay cup, never once drunk from while he reads, and he drinks now — the gesture tells the reader what the boy's sentence cost the man before Cleon says a word about it.

l.59's restored exception is the strongest single sentence the repair produced: 'that debt stood, and the twelfth was told because the eleventh was not yet.' The covenant paragraph no longer claims a perfect record; it claims a man paying one debt because another is open, which is a harder and truer thing and it costs the author nothing to say.
